newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BEBETO SCORES TWICE IN VITORIA FIGHTBACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BEBETO SCORES TWICE IN VITORIA FIGHTBACK.

text.p: Brazil veteran Bebeto scored two goals and went to the top of the Brazilian championship goalscoring table as Vitoria drew 3-3 with local rivals Bahia on Sunday.

Bebeto, who has made no secret of the fact that he wants to play for his country in next year's World Cup, took his tally in the competition to eight goals in five games and is joint top-scorer with Sao Paulo's Dodo.
He struck either side of halftime as the team came from two goals behind in a derby against Bahia in the northeastern city of Salvador. The match was played before a 90,000 crowd.
Bebeto was one of the heroes as Brazil won the last World Cup and even though he will be 34 by the time of next year's tournament, he is not counting himself out of the squad.
His last appearance for Brazil was in the Olympic Games in Atlanta.
Portuguesa, runners-up last year, went top of the table after handing former leaders Parana their first defeat of the competition. Striker Alex Alves scored the only goal of the game.

Defending champions Gremio recorded their first win of the tournament at the seventh attempt as they beat Juventude 1-0 away, despite playing most of the second half with ten men after midfielder Otacilio was sent off.
Luis Carlos Goiano, one of the few members of last year's side still at the club, scored the only goal.
Gremio have been Brazil's most successful team in the last three years but are now paying the price for selling off most of their players.
Despite Sunday's win, they are still fourth from bottom.

Flamengo, playing their first game since the departure of Romario, were beaten 1-0 by Rio de Janeiro rivals Vasco da Gama in another derby. Romario was playing on loan from Spanish club Valencia, but the deal expired last week.
